name: Journaling for Clarity & Productivity
instructions: Spend 5-10 minutes writing freely about what is on your mind, without editing or worrying about how it sounds.
End with three lines: one win from today, one thing that did not go well, and one thing to try differently tomorrow.
Keep it low-pressure -- a few honest sentences are more valuable than a perfectly composed entry.
Watch today's video for how journaling can support both clarity and productivity.
